statement: For a base $b > 0$ with $b \neq 1$, the logarithm of a number $x > 0$ to base $b$, written $\log_b x$, is the unique real number $y$ such that $b^y = x$. Equivalently, the logarithm function $\log_b\colon \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the inverse function of exponentiation $f(x) = b^x$.

symbols.meaning: base of the logarithm, a positive real number not equal to 1
argument of the logarithm, a positive real number
logarithm value (the exponent such that b^y = x)
base-b logarithm function, inverse to exponentiation with base b

properties.property: Inverse of exponentiation: \log_b(b^x) = x for all x \in \mathbb{R} and b^{\log_b x} = x for all x > 0
properties.why: The logarithm to base b is defined as the inverse of exponentiation with base b

properties.property: Product formula: \log_b(x y) = \log_b x + \log_b y for x, y > 0
properties.why: Follows from the properties of exponentiation where multiplying powers corresponds to adding exponents

properties.property: Quotient formula: \log_b(c / d) = \log_b c - \log_b d for positive numbers c and d
properties.why: Division of arguments corresponds to subtraction of their logarithms

properties.property: Power formula: \log_b(c^d) = d \log_b c (and \ln(t^r) = r \ln t)
properties.why: Exponentiation of the argument reduces to multiplication by the exponent
Follows from the derivative of the exponential function and the chain rule for inverse functions

properties.property: Integral representation of the natural logarithm: \ln t = \int_1^t \frac{1}{x}\,dx for t > 0
properties.why: The natural logarithm ln(x) is the unique antiderivative of 1/x that has the value 0 for x = 1

assumptions.assumption: Base b is a positive real number unequal to 1 (b > 0, b != 1)
assumptions.breaks_when: b <= 0 (exponential function is not well-defined on all real numbers) or b = 1 (f(x) = 1^x is constant and not bijective)

assumptions.assumption: Argument x is a positive real number (x > 0)
assumptions.breaks_when: x <= 0, since the range of the real exponential function b^y is R_{>0}

failure_modes.signature: Divergence as x -> 0+ (to -infinity for b > 1, or +infinity for b < 1); undefined for x <= 0
failure_modes.cause: No real exponent y satisfies b^y <= 0 for positive b

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero in derivative formula (ln 1 = 0); non-invertible mapping
failure_modes.cause: f(x) = 1^x = 1 is constant, so it fails the strict monotonicity condition required for bijectivity

failure_modes.signature: Exponentiation cannot be defined as a continuous bijection from R to R_{>0}
failure_modes.cause: Powers with non-positive bases are not generally real-valued across the real line
